subsystems.name: Spin sensor
subsystems.role: a transducer that converts a tiny nuclear magnetic signal into a measurable electrical or optical one.

subsystems.name: Polarisation and excitation
subsystems.role: makes the nuclear spins visible by aligning them, then flips them with resonant pulses.
parts: hyperpolarisation stage (dynamic nuclear polarisation or optical pumping)

subsystems.name: Encoding gradients
subsystems.role: turns position into a measurable frequency so the signal can be mapped in three dimensions.
parts: gradient coils or the field profile of the tip itself

subsystems.name: Readout
subsystems.role: extracts a signal from a single spin or a handful of spins.
parts: optical interferometer or laser and photodetector

subsystems.name: Environment
subsystems.role: silences thermal noise so weak signals survive.

subsystems.name: Sample handling and control
subsystems.role: places nanometre-scale specimens or surfaces at the correct distance from the sensor.

buildSteps.title: Make the sensor
buildSteps.detail: A diamond is grown by chemical vapour deposition with a controlled density of nitrogen-vacancy centres a few nanometres below the surface, or silicon cantilevers a few hundred nanometres thick are patterned by lithography.

buildSteps.title: Attach the signal source
buildSteps.detail: A magnetic particle or thin magnetic film tens of nanometres across is fixed to the cantilever tip, or a shallow nitrogen-vacancy centre is positioned within about 10 nm of the sample surface.

buildSteps.title: Cold-launch and evacuate
buildSteps.detail: The assembly enters high vacuum and millikelvin temperatures, both to keep the cantilever from being damped by gas or to keep the diamond defect's spin coherence long.

buildSteps.title: Polarise the nuclear spins
buildSteps.detail: Microwaves or laser light transfer order from electrons to nuclei, boosting the otherwise minuscule thermal polarisation by orders of magnitude.

buildSteps.title: Approach the sample
buildSteps.detail: The sensor is brought within nanometres of the specimen while an interferometer or confocal microscope tracks its position and deflection.

buildSteps.title: Excite and encode
buildSteps.detail: Radio-frequency pulses flip nuclei at a chosen resonance, and the magnetic field gradient makes that resonance depend on position along each axis.

buildSteps.title: Detect the resonance
buildSteps.detail: The cantilever deflection or the defect's fluorescence is monitored while the excitation frequency sweeps; the resulting shift is the nuclear magnetic resonance signature.

buildSteps.title: Reconstruct the volume
buildSteps.detail: Signals recorded at many sensor positions and frequencies are inverted by computer into a three-dimensional map of chemical species.

prerequisites.why: without them, thermal motion drowns out forces at the attonewton scale and shortens spin coherence.

prerequisites.tech: Nanoscale magnetic tips and field gradients
prerequisites.why: spatial resolution scales with gradient strength, and practical tips reach only so far.
thermal polarisation at these fields is far too weak to detect a few nuclei without it.

prerequisites.tech: Coherent control and readout of nitrogen-vacancy centres
prerequisites.why: shallow defects lose coherence to surface noise, the main limit on sensitivity.

prerequisites.tech: Single-spin quantum metrology and noise suppression
prerequisites.why: detecting one proton requires averaging and decoupling schemes still under development.

pathway.milestone: proof-of-concept imaging of viruses and proteins with nanometre resolution
pathway.unlocks: confidence that magnetic resonance can beat its conventional diffraction limit.

pathway.milestone: routine single-molecule nuclear magnetic resonance at surfaces
pathway.unlocks: non-destructive chemical identification of individual molecules and surface species.

pathway.milestone: shallow defects with long coherence times and better hyperpolarised samples
pathway.unlocks: shorter measurement times and chemical sensitivity approaching conventional spectroscopy.

pathway.milestone: commercial instruments for structural biology and materials science
pathway.unlocks: routine atomic-scale structure determination without crystallisation or staining.
